The Fourier kernel of the support is derived by explicit orthogonality, with the even-dimensional balanced shell evaluated by an exact generating identity. Absolute-value signs, 2^{-2n} normalization, and sharp convolution equality are handled explicitly. The previously known multiplier spectrum is used as a verified input; the new mathematical check is the exact l1/l∞ projection-kernel evaluation. The full integer transform and exact norms are independently tested by graph enumeration in check.py for n=2..8; the general proof does not rely on finite tests.

originality.rationale: An accessible earlier result for exactly K_{2,n} already establishes all Walsh multipliers, zero set, rank, and the sharp norm of the distinct projection onto tree-incidence frequencies; those conclusions are not claimed as new. The final novelty claim is limited to the sharp l1/l∞ norm of the projection onto the NONZERO WALSH SUPPORT (range of convolution), with its exact even/odd formulas and growth dichotomy. The previous spectrum makes this new projection well-defined and evaluable in principle, but it does not contain the balanced-shell Krawtchouk absolute-kernel summation or its closed value. Inspecting the pertinent literature and published-finding corpus search returned no coverage of this particular sharp norm. General weighted tree formulas, classical binomial identities, and prior spectrum formulas are acknowledged inputs. Historical priority remains bounded.

value.rationale: The complete Walsh spectrum of K_{2,n} spanning trees is previously known; the newly evaluated invariant is the sharp l1/l∞ norm of the canonical projection onto the convolution range. It quantifies stability of retaining all nonzero observable Fourier modes and differs mathematically from the earlier projection indexed by spanning-tree frequencies. Exact evaluation exhibits a large parity phase transition, from order sqrt(n) to order 2^{n/2}/sqrt(n), which is not obtained from merely counting Fourier zeros. The balanced-shell cancellation/absolute-value computation is structurally motivated and applies for every n>=2.
